findings.claim: Today, around six million pilgrims visit Lourdes each year
findings.truth: The sanctuary receives about four million visitors a year; the six-million figure is an old, inflated one.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes (around four million tourists every year)

findings.claim: Lourdes attracts around six million pilgrims per year (4-mark mark scheme)
findings.truth: About four million a year, as F1.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes

findings.claim: Christians celebrate Christmas on 25 December (though Orthodox Christians celebrate on 7 January)
findings.truth: Only the Orthodox churches that keep the Julian calendar celebrate on 7 January; Greek, Romanian and other Orthodox churches keep 25 December.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Christmas (part of the Eastern Orthodox churches use the Old Style date)

findings.claim: Card 4 front 'In _____ a 14-year-old girl named Bernadette Soubirous reported 18 visions...' with the answer '1858'
findings.truth: A cloze fragment that starts with a blank and has no question word. Rewritten as 'Who reported 18 visions of the Virgin Mary at Lourdes in 1858?' / 'Bernadette Soubirous', which also stops it repeating knowledge check 1.
findings.evidence: docs/FLASHCARD_RULES.md validator rules (single-word answers, fragments)

findings.claim: The Trussell Trust ... runs over 1,400 food bank centres across the UK
findings.truth: Trussell supports a network of about 1,700 food bank centres (2024-25); the centres are run locally, not by the Trust.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Trussell Trust (1,711 centres, April 2024 - March 2025; supports a network)

findings.claim: It now operates in over 300 locations across the UK (Street Pastors)
findings.truth: Street Pastors runs in about 250 towns and cities in the UK, with roughly 8,000 volunteers.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Street Pastors (approximately 250 towns and cities, 2023)

findings.claim: Christian Aid works with communities of all faiths and none in around 37 countries
findings.truth: Christian Aid works in 24 countries.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Christian Aid

findings.claim: Match answer: 'Works with communities of all faiths in around 37 countries'

findings.claim: CAFOD is funded mainly by Catholic parishes.
findings.truth: CAFOD's income comes from the Catholic community (parishes and schools), the public, institutional donors and UK government aid; parish giving is not the main source.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, CAFOD (funding sources, 2022/23 income)

findings.claim: For 5-mark 'Explain Two' questions on mission or world poverty...
findings.truth: The paper sets five-part questions worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 5-mark question; the 'explain two, refer to a source' question is worth 6 marks, as the lesson's own practice questions say.

findings.claim: 'Give one ways Christian charities work to help world poverty.' labelled 1 mark, with a scheme reading '1 marks for each valid way, up to 2 marks'
findings.truth: The short recall question is worth 1 mark and the paper has no 2-mark question. Question and scheme rewritten to the unit's house shape: name two ways, one mark for two correct points.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1; lessons 1-4 of this unit

findings.claim: disciples: 'The training of new converts in the Christian faith, encouraging them to spread the gospel and supporting fellow believers.' (glossary term, in-text definition and flashcard answer)
findings.truth: That defines discipleship, not disciples. Disciples are followers of Jesus who learn from his teaching and pass it on.
findings.evidence: standard usage; the lesson's own sentence ('people who actively follow his teachings')

findings.claim: 'Faith without action is dead' (James 2:17), quoted again as James 2:26 in the conclusion, the knowledge check and two mark schemes
findings.truth: No standard translation reads that way. James 2:26 reads 'faith without deeds is dead'; James 2:17 reads 'faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead'. Standardised on the verbatim wording and reference.
findings.evidence: Bible Gateway, James 2 (NIV)

findings.claim: 12-mark scheme ladder 'Top band (10-12) / Upper-mid band (7-9) / Lower-mid band (4-6) / Lower band (1-3)'
findings.truth: Those ranges do not match the 12-mark ladder used everywhere else in the unit and 'Lower band' is not a house band name. Replaced with the single house line used by lessons 1-4, which also states the 3 SPaG marks.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1 and 4.5 (SPaG, up to 3 marks on the 12-mark question); lessons 1-4

findings.claim: 6-mark schemes: 'Award up to 3 marks for the first reason and 2 marks for the second (or vice versa). 1 mark for a relevant reference to sacred writings or Christian teaching for each reason.'
findings.truth: That totals seven marks on a six-mark question, and contradicts the line above it. Replaced with the house line used by lessons 1-4 (3 marks per reason, the third for a source).
findings.evidence: recomputation; lessons 1-4 of this unit

findings.claim: Card 4 front 'Key Fact _____ means “sent out” ...' with the answer 'Mission', repeating card 1's answer
findings.truth: The card carried a scraped 'Key Fact' label and duplicated card 1 in the same deck. Replaced with 'Where in the Bible is the Great Commission recorded?' / 'Matthew 28:16-20'.
findings.evidence: docs/FLASHCARD_RULES.md (no duplicate answers in a deck; no fragments)

findings.claim: Worldwide, around 80,000 people become Christians each day, and over 500 new churches begin.
findings.truth: An unattributed evangelical statistic. Global Christian growth of roughly 25-30 million a year puts it in the right order, but no neutral source states it, so it should not be quoted as a fact in an exam answer.
findings.evidence: no neutral source found (WebSearch budget exhausted)

findings.claim: It celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, three days after his crucifixion.
findings.truth: The traditional and creedal wording is 'on the third day'; Good Friday to Easter Sunday is two days later. Not worth an edit, but 'on the third day' is the safer phrase.
findings.evidence: the lesson's own glossary entry ('on the third day after his crucifixion')

summary: Lessons 1 and 2 are clean: every scripture quotation, reference and denominational claim checked out, and the exam claims match the spec's 1/1/4/6/12 structure with 3 SPaG marks on the 12-mark question. Lesson 5 carries the serious faults - a 5-mark question type that does not exist, a 1-mark question whose scheme awarded 2, a definition of 'disciples' that actually defines discipleship, and a misquoted James reference repeated in five places. Lessons 3 and 4 needed charity and site figures refreshed (Lourdes visitors, Trussell, Street Pastors, Christian Aid) and four broken cloze flashcards rebuilt. Separate observation, not edited: every deck in this unit runs definition-front, term-back, which FLASHCARD_RULES.md names as an interference anti-pattern and which leaves single-word answers such as 'worship', 'sacrament' and 'pilgrimage' on fronts that are not questions.
